title: Evaluated simultaneous derived reduction factors through residue sheaves
statement: Let ell be prime and W any scheme. Let D be a simultaneous derived reduction of the scalar-extension functor from integral abelian pro-etale sheaves to discrete constant Z_ell-module sheaves, as in [def-sfb-diagonal-system-interface]. For every natural number n and the displayed derived-category universe choices, there exists a functor R from the derived category of integral abelian sheaves to the derived category of constant Z/ell^(n+1)-module sheaves, together with a natural isomorphism between R followed by exact coefficient restriction and D.T followed by exact evaluation at n. No endpoint objects or Ext classes are involved.

source.place: Step (2), common-resolution computation, and step (4), evaluation with residue coefficients before restriction.

proof.text: The p-adic projection to Z/ell^(n+1) is surjective and has principal kernel generated by ell^(n+1). The proved source-library Sheaf.reductionDatum constructs residue reduction as sheafification of the quotient by this kernel. Compose it with integral-to-p-adic scalar extension. After restriction its projection is a cokernel of positive-power multiplication; the unique cokernel comparison identifies it naturally with D.ordinary evaluated at n.

Use the proved helpers of [lem-sfb-diagonal-derived-reduction-exists]. The common resolving class consists of complexes on which every positive ell-power acts monomorphically termwise. Flat-term K-flat resolutions resolve every complex by this class. Scalar extension is exact, and the quotient short exact sequences show that both the tower functor and its level functor invert quasi-isomorphisms within this class. Restriction is exact and reflects quasi-isomorphisms, so the residue functor inverts them too.

The same cochain resolving-class construction gives universal left-derived functors for the tower, level and residue functors, with counits invertible on the resolving class. Uniqueness identifies the supplied D with the tower construction, so its counit is also invertible there. Compose counits with exact-functor localization comparisons for evaluation and restriction. A left-derived universal property gives natural transformations from each resulting composite to the derived level functor. They are isomorphisms on the common resolving class and hence on every derived object, since every derived object is isomorphic to the localization of one such resolution. Composing one comparison with the inverse of the other gives the asserted factorization.

lean.statement:
theorem diagonal_residue_derived_factorization (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (W : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (DiagonalAb W)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (DiagonalSystems ℓ W)]
    (n : ℕ)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wB} (DiagonalMod ℓ W)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wC}
      (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology W) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (diagonalResidue.{u} ℓ n)))]
    (D : DiagonalDerivedReduction ℓ (diagonalScalarExtension ℓ W)) :
    ∃ R : DerivedCategory (DiagonalAb W) ⥤
        DerivedCategory
          (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology W) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (diagonalResidue.{u} ℓ n))),
      Nonempty (R ⋙ (diagonalFiniteToPadic ℓ n W).mapDerivedCategory ≅
        D.T ⋙ ((evaluation ℕᵒᵖ (DiagonalMod ℓ W)).obj (op n)).mapDerivedCategory)
